The `CaDiskLifecycle` TLA+ model's v1 state machine contains `Live`, `Transient`, `IdentityLost`, `VanishedReplaced`, and `VanishedForgotten`; it has no `VanishedErased` state.

FORGET is modeled in this order: mutex acquisition, idempotent `isVanished` short-circuit, intent publication, trip 1, GC stop and join, remount stop and join, trip 2, drain, `finishTeardown`, `keeperReset`, `enterVanished(Forgotten)`, and mutex release.
[C1] requires `loop()` and `heartbeatLoop()` to check `isVanished()` at each wake and self-exit, preventing new GC rounds after `Vanished`.
[M1] requires the remount attempt's step-0 bail to check `vanished_intent` as well as `isVanished()`.
[M1] prevents new remount attempts after intent publication, but an attempt that passed its bail may finish reclaim inside FORGET's join window; trip 2 closes that race.

The modeled `ForgetTerminal` invariant requires completed FORGET to have a latched fence and a `Vanished` state; removing trip 2 violates it because an in-flight reclaim can restore `Live` and `mayMutate() == TRUE`.
The modeled `ForgetWinsUnlessNatural` invariant makes the final state `VanishedForgotten` unless a natural `Replaced` transition wins the first-terminal-wins latch.
The modeled `EarnedFarewell` invariant permits farewell only after a provable drain, and `OneWay` forbids transitions from `IdentityLost` or `Vanished` back to `Live` or `Transient`.
The modeled `GcStoppedAfterForget` invariant holds even on idempotent FORGET and post-FORGET `GC START`, because the Admin gate refuses GC on a non-`Live` pool.

Manifest-body redundancy is entirely cross-transaction; an op- or transaction-scoped cache saves nothing, while a round-scoped cache can avoid two round trips per avoided edge because each fetch uses HEAD plus GET.
The HEAD-before-GET pair is a protocol step and must not be removed as a cheap performance optimization.
